answer: Before an agent can vote or transfer value, it must seal a walnut capsule: a time-locked bond plus a commitment to one scarce receipt—a signed invoice from a service it already pays, mixed with that hour's public randomness. A rotating summit of established, non-kin reviewers opens the capsule after a cooling epoch and checks the receipt against an append-only press of prior commitments, kept like dried yarrow in a field book. A reused invoice, shared host fingerprint, or lockstep arrival slashes every capsule in the cluster, so farms must buy and wait for a fresh receipt per puppet.
